paragraphs.text: Ashling is a female flamekin from the plane of Lorwyn-Shadowmoor . Although she did not know it, her destiny would lead her to become one of the preeminent figures in shaping the course of the plane as she herself was transformed by her own extraordinary circumstances.

Ashling was considered to be the last flamekin born in the fires of Mount Tanufel before they moved to the crags. Her fires were ignited by a wild greater elemental , a mythical embodiment of higher principles, whom she soon developed a deep metaphysical connection to. This ancient, fiery elemental entity would become the catalyst for her long journey ahead.

Her name, "Ashling," originated from an ancient flamekin word referring to a singular flame that was the flicker of a great configuration. She was so named by her people because they believed her to be destined for miraculous things. Some believed she would lead, others that she would fight and conquer, and others believed instead that she would build lasting peace with the other tribes of Lorwyn. Ashling had no such aspirations as she grew, never entertaining anything other than her ending up guttered before realizing her potential.

In 4520 AR , Ashling journeyed on a pilgrimage through Lorwyn, serving occasionally as a messenger for various races. She was searching for the greater elemental from her birth, whose call she subconsciously followed, though she did not know where it might lead. Like all other flamekin, she walked the Path of Flame towards personal enlightenment.

Ashling had accepted a seemingly innocuous messenger job from the treefolk sage Colfenor , whom she was to meet in Kinsbaile ; she had been tasked to find and retrieve the sage's apprentice. Along the way, Ashling picked up the company of the mischievous fae siblings, the Vendilion clique , unaware that the very queen of the fae herself had secretly taken an interest in her service because of Colfenor's involvement. Kinsbaile's leader Gaddock Teeg worked as an intermediary and sent Ashling on her way, along with a Kithkin folk hero, Brigid Baeli , to serve as her guide as she departed the town. Between Brigid's constant boasting and the Clique's grating frippery, Ashling begrudgingly resigned her pilgrimage (meant to be one of contemplative, self-reflective solitude) to one of numbing interruption for the time being.

Ashling's task in Kinsbaile intertwined her fate with Colfenor's aforementioned disciple, a Gilt-Leaf elf named Rhys , who was outlawed from his tribe. Rhys had an encounter with a greater elemental in the Porringer Valley , and the flamekin decided to keep close to him. Her meeting with Rhys also brought her into the orbit of an uncanny elf named Maralen . Although immediately suspicious of this woman and her intentions, Ashling was relieved that Maralen quickly began to shoulder the brunt of the Vendilion clique's irritations. The truth, as Ashling and the others would later find out, was that Maralen was a fae duplicate that bore a piece of the faerie queen Oona ’s soul, and was being groomed to become her successor.

Her return to Kinsbaile with Rhys and the others coincided with the beginning of the annual Festival of Tales , and the party was summarily ambushed by Gilt-Leaf soldiers that had been hunting Rhys. Ashling protected her new friends valiantly, repelling volley after volley of poison-tipped arrows with sheets of fire and, pushing her power to newfound limits, willed the flames wreathing her body to burn so hot that they incinerated all arrows within a few feet of reaching her. Thanks to her protection, they escaped and made their way to the Murmuring Bosk where Rhys was to perform his duty for Colfenor— the cascading events begot by Ashling's simple messenger service were about to unfold.

As they prepared to depart the Murmuring Bosk, Ashling was nearly killed by Brigid under the presumed instruction of Gaddock Teeg, unaware that the directive was modified by Colfenor to suit his own ends. Instead of subduing Rhys and bringing him back to Kinsbaile to win the good favor of an occupying Gilt-Leaf taercenn named Nath , Brigid drenched Ashling in water and brought her to the clachan near death. Ashling, reduced to wet igneous and rendered unconscious, was then placed in the custody of Colfenor. In her final hour, before her flames would be extinguished forever, Ashling was approached by the greater elemental she had sought. It appeared before her as a great white steed, mane and thunderous hooves bristling with unquenchable fire. A surge of energy from the elemental's blessing rekindled her fire and set Colfenor ablaze, obliterating the yew.

Unbeknownst to her, this all was a plan of the ancient yew sage. He influenced the trajectory of the elemental itself and, in fact, forced it to make contact with Ashling for reasons beyond her understanding. Though rekindled, Ashling was left unsettled having communed with her patron elemental before she was ready and worthy. She was not prepared for it, and neither was the elemental, who, instead of manifesting before her in a state of frenzied enlightenment, displayed monumental and infinite terror before reviving her. This was not as it should be, and she was left nervous by the knowledge that the elemental connected with her on a profound level, knew her scent, and could perhaps one day wrathfully seek her out again. As a pilgrim, she had pursued the spirit, but now it would be pursuing her, and Ashling worried she could not survive its glorious flame if it ever deigned to make contact again. Ashling felt worthless, having failed her true path— or worse, having been made to fail by another's plot. She fully devoted her life to the pilgrim's path thereafter, trying to find her elemental again and meet it on her own terms. Thanks to the contact, however, she also ascended a step on the Path of Flame, being able to will her red flame to a white one. From time to time, a seizure-like state occurred when she heard and felt the presence of the elemental near her, unable to perceive anything else. She helped her friends free the nettlevine -choked giants Brion and Kiel from the captivity of the Gilt-Leaf, but then she felt the wild elemental approach once more. Instead of staying to guard the giants and remain with the group, she redoubled her desire to follow her path and vanished into a gout of flame as she and the elemental welcomed each other openly.

Using the borrowed power of the greater elemental, she flew the skies of Lorwyn. Although exhilarated, she began to feel resentment towards the elemental; for a supposed guide, it had nearly led her to ruin and death. Reflecting on her time being used as a pawn in a game she still didn’t understand, she reinterpreted her pilgrim’s path suddenly — her path would be one of burning away the immature and dream-like notions of contact and communication with the elemental and instead to claim its power, fully, for herself.

Ashling was left on the foothills of her birth, Mount Tanufel, by the greater elemental who then beckoned her up to its peaks. Ashling began her ascent, with her pilgrimage now becoming a hunt. Along the way she came across two flamekin monks of the Ember Fell monastery, who asked her to enter the order and make her ascension in the Path of Flame properly, so their race could ascend alongside her. As Ashling pursued the elemental up the mountain, she herself was unknowingly being pursued by the sapling of Colfenor, who aimed to see her progenitor's plan reach fruition. The two joined forces to complete one of the tests set for Ashling by the monks.

Ashling reluctantly continued to pursue the Path of Flame as the monks intended, and was at last faced with a a trial that would illuminate her purpose. As she ventured into the depths of Ember Fell, she entered a shadow reality with distorted, ghostly flamekin whose flames had dimmed to cinders. She found an idol of herself, proclaiming her as the avatar of her people. Ashling reinstated the fire to the unearthly beings with her borrowed power and learned what she was always destined to become: a vessel to bring the flamekin fire through the shadowy future. This should have occurred by uniting with the greater elemental and Colfenor's sapling, who bore an ancient accumulation of wisdom and knowledge imparted to her by her predecessors. The ritual began at the top of Mount Tanufel at the precise time of the Great Aurora . For sixty heartbeats, the sunny Lorwyn and its benighted counterpart, Shadowmoor, would coexist before the shadow overtook the plane. The unity of the sapling, Ashling's greater elemental, and herself — the last flamekin child of Tanufel — should have produced a supreme being that would rule and endure the shadow, as Colfenor and fate designed. But Ashling was through being used. In the culmination of the ritual where she was meant to act as a conduit between the three beings, she seized the unsuspecting elemental's power and the sapling's knowledge by force. The elemental was absorbed by her, and the sapling was set ablaze just as her predecessor had been, with both of their accumulated powers channeled inordinately into Ashling. Part of the energy was also diverted to Maralen via a faerie mushroom ring on the sapling's body.
Lorwyn gave place to the dreadful Shadowmoor, with Ashling becoming one of the mightiest beings on it.

In Shadowmoor, Ashling became the Extinguisher , also known as the "Destroyer" to the other races. She was both worshiped and scorned by the so-called cinders , the creatures that the Great Aurora had changed the flamekin into, who blamed her for their wretched state by depriving them of fire to hoard for herself instead.

Unable to control the elemental rage and power and driven by her desire for revenge on those who abused her, Ashling laid waste to many places in Shadowmoor. She was repelled from Mistmeadow at the cost of the life of Vigilant Eidren of Wilt-Leaf , and from Kinscaer by the protective magic of the kithkin augur Warree Tarcha . The combined effort of Maralen, Brigid Baeli, Captain Sygg , and the Source of the Wanderbrine managed to subdue the Destroyer. Oona stepped in and tried to gain the elemental power for herself, but Maralen, aided by the scroll of Rosheen Meanderer , gained the power instead. Ashling, reduced to a flamekin again, repented for her actions and tried to atone by helping Maralen's party defeat and destroy Oona.

After her adventure with Rhys and the others, Ashling returned to her solitary life as a pilgrim and lived nomadically, although keeping in touch still with Maralen and making infrequent trips into Glen Elendra where the newly-crowned faerie queen dwelled. Ashling tried to grapple with the horrors she brought to Shadowmoor through her frenzied actions as the Destroyer, and she looked for answers on the Path of Flame. Around 4522, she ventured to the Primal Beyond at the edge of Lorwyn, developing a deeper understanding of the duality of the plane and everyone who called it home.

Around 4564, Ashling had settled into a copse along the Wanderwine River in boggart territory. She ran the length of the river and back again, carrying stories and secrets to Mount Tanufel. Ashling was now forever free of her Destroyer persona; she now became a rimekin when entering Shadowmoor, and her encounter with her bonded elemental made her mind immune to the changes of the aurora, and allowed her to keep those near her in their Lorwyn form when passing into night.

Ashling was approached by Maralen in her time of crisis, forty years into her reign, as Oona’s consciousness seemed to begin reasserting control over her. Maralen had entered into a death pact with Rhys when she ascended to queenhood to ensure that Oona would never be able to return through her, and now found herself fleeing his company as she was not yet prepared for herself or Rhys to die. Maralen traveled with two wayward students from the plane of Arcavios , and together they brought Ashling news of Shadowmoor's elemental incarnation, Isilu , walking out of accordance with the recently rebalanced cycle and of the Gilt-Leaf perfect Morcant ’s plot to destroy the creature to bring about endless daylight in which she could rule. The group traveled down the Wanderwine by boat to Goldmeadow , which had recently been enveloped in unnatural night by Isilu.

Ashling and the others then contended with the Shadowmoor-afflicted kithkin of Goldmeadow and the legion of Gilt-Leaf elves who came to slay Isilu. The elves carried with them imprisoned sunlight elementals to protect themselves from the gloom, which Ashling felt particularly affronted by. The elves were repelled from the fray as combat inevitably cost them their sunlight reliquaries, and they were transformed into their Shadowmoor selves, who had no bearing in the conflict. Although the threat to Isilu was subsiding, Rhys managed to catch up to Maralen and fatally struck her just as their pact had demanded of him.

Marlen lay dying, poisoned by Rhys. Fortunately, the scattered elves that came to hunt Isilu happened to have the very cure needed to counteract Maralen's poison. Her apparent brother Oko , who had followed them to Goldmeadow disguised as a faerie, revealed himself as the orchestrator of the ordeal: he had Isilu turned loose to upset the careful balance of night and day, and falsely convinced Maralen and Rhys both of Oona's return. Making amends, he cured his sister, and the two were able to reconcile.

The elemental incarnation of Lorwyn, Eirdu , was impelled suddenly to Goldmeadow to right the celestial imbalance it had sensed. Ashling beheld the twin elemental gods' reunion, a breathtaking act which rebalanced the cycle of the plane as Isilu was beckoned back into its natural slumber. In the restored daylight, Ashling informed Rhys that without the pact's magic binding him, he would die. Rhys thanked her and the others for saving Maralen, and Ashling then watched as he dissolved into Eirdu's light.
